Gdyby się ogień z nieostrożności czego Boże zachowaj wsi znaj— — dował, a z domowych, sąsiadów, który nie chciał do ratunku i gaszenia przybyć, ten powinien na trzy dobre grzywny być [ukarany]. 12. Kto by przy ogniu cudzą siekierę, topór, albo węborek, motykę czyli naczynie jakie cudze wziął, ten rzeczy te powinien do sołtysa przynieść 1 to u niego złożyć, żeby się wróciło, komu należy, pod karą grzywny dobrej jednej.

</div>
<div class="lit-en" lang="en" markdown="1">

2. If a neighbour addresses the sołtys or his ławniks in discourteous or abusive words, or threatens them with a weapon, and when he comes to court refuses to listen, he is to be fined two good grzywny without any [exception]. If he then behaves worse still, or threatens blows, he is to be sentenced by their judgement to a heavier penalty.

3. But if anyone boldly and violently attacks the sołtys or his ławniks, and having given rein to his anger [fol. 6] refuses to obey, or will not submit, then whoever beats or wounds him in that event, by day or by night, goes free and incurs no penalty, nor is any court needed.

4. Whoever is sent by the sołtys on official business, and anyone presumes to abuse or beat him, shall be fined two good grzywny.

5. When the sołtys holds court with the ławniks, no woman is to be present, unless she herself has some complaint of her own, or her husband is not at home. Otherwise a woman who offends in this is to pay a fine of five groszes.

6. I permit that each year they are to pay the sołtys thirty groszes from every huba for his trouble and toil, and his ławniks fifteen groszes each year. Whoever opposes this is to be punished in duplo [twice over].

7. If the sołtys and the ławniks make any journey on the community's business and for the good of their estate, the costs are to be taken from the hubas according to the account.

8. The sołtys and the ławniks are to watch carefully over the good of the whole village and community, to take care of the fences, dams, ditches and sluices, and wherever harm might come to the community, to block, repair and put it right. If the sołtys and the ławniks are negligent in this, they are to be punished at the discretion of the whole community.

9. When there is any purchase of grain or of cattle, and a sealing drink (litkup) has already been drunk at the purchase, the party who does not keep the bargain is to give a barrel of beer as a penalty.

10. God forbid that a building should catch fire and burn down through a thunderbolt or through the doing of wicked men; the neighbours are then to help him out of Christian charity — each huba contributing, at 100 grzywny, the 15th grosz, according to the assessment of the damage — and they are to help him with timber, reed and carting.

11. God forbid that a fire from carelessness should break out in the village, in one of the houses: any neighbour who will not come to the rescue and to the extinguishing is to be [fined] three good grzywny.

12. Whoever at a fire takes someone else's axe, hatchet, weborek [?], hoe or any other utensil belonging to another, is to bring those things to the sołtys and deposit them with him, so that they may be returned to their owner, on pain of a fine of one good grzywna.

Powinien jeden drugiemu do zbudowaniai wyporządzenia podwórza gnojem i wodą, jeżeli tego potrzeba, służyć. Kto by tego czynić nie chciał, przepada na karę grzywny dobrej jednej. 17. Należyta granica zaś być taka: rowie pół pręta albo laski ma w szeroka, dwa łokcie głęboka. Płot albo zagrodzenie ma być dwa łokcie wysoki, tak żeby półletnie cielę przezeń nie przelazło. Przy tym, gdyby się [we] wsi znajdował koń albo bydło rogate, które by płoty psuło i -przeskakiwało, powinni temu zapobiec, albo bydło takie zbyć. Trzydzieści zaś rózg albo prętów powinno być podwórza domostwem, ogrodem, stajniami dla bydła, świń, kur, gęsI z z 1 kaczek, dobrze opatrzone. 22. Gdyby komu konia, wołu albo krowę ukradzioro, powinni sąsiedzi starania dołożyć, aby się kradzicż taka wydała i znalazła.

</div>
<div class="lit-en" lang="en" markdown="1">

13. No one is to presume to go and challenge another before his porch or his door. Whoever does this incurs a fine of three good grzywny.

14. If anyone presumes to waylay another on the road, in the field or in the village, and this can be proved by two reputable witnesses, he is to be punished according to the assessment of the seriousness of the matter. [fol. 7]

15. If one neighbour reviles another, or women abuse one another with unseemly words, to the damage of their honour, and there are two steady witnesses, they are to be fined two good grzywny; the unseemly words [are to] be proved, or honour made good, at the discretion of the court.

16. One neighbour is to help another with manure and water in the building and fitting out of his farmyard, when this is needed. Whoever will not do this is liable to a fine of one good grzywna.

17. If a neighbour opens an enclosure or a fence and does not close it again, so that any damage results, he is to make good that damage and pay a fine of one grzywna.

18. If anyone drives across another's sown field, he is to bear a fine of one grzywna and make good the damage.

19. If the sołtys orders the pastures to be cleaned, the boundaries to be finished, the outflow of the waters to be cleaned and sluiced, and whatever ditches may be useful to the village, whoever does not obey this order and does not do his part is liable to a fine of two grzywny and must complete the said work within a week, on pain of a double penalty.

20. One neighbour is to keep and maintain the boundaries of another, whether ditches or fences, as the place requires. Whoever does not do this, if damage results, is to make good and pay for the damage; and whatever complaint there may be, ten groszes always fall to the sołtys.

21. The proper boundary is to be as follows: a ditch is to be half a rod or a laska wide, and two ells deep. A fence or enclosure is to be two ells high, so that a half-year-old calf cannot climb over it. Moreover, if there is in the village a horse or horned cattle that spoil and jump the fences, this is to be prevented, or such cattle disposed of. There are to be thirty rządek or rods of farmyard, with the dwelling, the garden and the stables for the cattle, pigs, hens, geese and ducks, well provided.

22. If anyone's horse, ox or cow is stolen, the neighbours are to take pains that the theft is disclosed and found out.

Gdy ktokolwiek zajęte bydło bije albo rzuca, że się bydlęciu szkoda przez to stanie, powinien szkodę nagrodzić, a karany ma być na trzy grzywny dobre. \| 31. pieniądze powinien od tegoż nazad 33. Gdyby od sołtysa nakaz był świnie klockować, a tego kto zaniedba, że się przez to szkoda sąsiadowi dzieje, powinien od każdej świni 5 groszy fantowego wziąć [recte: dać].

<div class="lit-en" lang="en" markdown="1">

23. No one is to presume to refuse and take away labourers or hired men who have been engaged, without the consent of the man for whom they work, unless they are already released after payment. Whoever presumes to do this will be liable to a fine of one good grzywna. 4fol. 8]

24. Whoever presumes to refuse a neighbour a farmhand or a maidservant, or to buy them off, shall be fined one grzywna, and is to send the farmhand or the maid back to serve their former master.

25. If anyone impounds a neighbour's cattle to its harm, he is to water and guard it, so that it does not suffer or die. Whoever is the cause of this is to bear the damage.

26. When anyone's cattle is impounded, the sołtys has notice given to the owner of the cattle; when he leaves his cattle in the pound, he is to pay for the first night five groszes a head, for the second night ten groszes a head, and so on up to the fifth night, always doubling. If after the fifth night the cattle is not collected and redeemed, it is to be driven to the lord's farmyard.

27. No one is to presume to drive a neighbour's cattle into his own house; it is to be handed over at once to the sołtys or a ławnik, on pain of a fine of one grzywna.

28. The sołtys is entitled to a third part of the redemption money for impounded cattle.

Whoever has no money to redeem the cattle is to find those who will stand surety for him, and leave a twofold pledge, to the sołtys's satisfaction.

29. If anyone, when his cattle is impounded and driven to the sołtys, opposes this and wants to take the cattle back by force, he is to be fined two good grzywny.

30. If anyone beats impounded cattle or throws things at it, so that the animal suffers harm by it, he is to make good the damage and is to be fined three good grzywny.

31. No one is to milk impounded cattle, or make use of impounded horses, or ride on them. Whoever contravenes this is to be fined one grzywna.

32. When someone finds another's cattle in his corn or in his meadow, he is to have the ławniks inspect and assess the damage; if he will not have this done, he is to be content with the customary redemption money, namely a grosz a head of cattle. For the inspection he is to pay the ławniks twelve imperial groszes, which they are to take on every occasion.

33. If the sołtys orders the pigs to be hobbled (klockować), and anyone neglects this, so that damage results to a neighbour, he is to take [recte: give] 5 groszes a pig for the impounding.

(fol 9] 34. Gęsi i kaczki, gdy szkodę sągiadowi wchodzą, wolno je zabić 1 komu należą, do domu odesłać. 35. Ważąc się który podczas sądu komu niepolitycznymi słowy fukać \| albo szalbierstwo zadać, powinien pięć groszy sztrafy położyć, gdyby zaś odgrażał biciem, powinien na posłuszeństwo pójść i gro-' szy 10 położyć. Zaś prędzej wypuszczony z posłuszeństwa być nie ma, póki się z sąsiadem swoim nie zgodzi i przeprosi. 36. Wiertel, kwarta i miara piwna ma być sprawiedliwa według miast sąsiedzkich odmierzona,. żeby się nikomu krzywda nie uczyniła. Kto naprzeciw temu czyni, a bliźniego swego oszuka, ma być według uznania sołtysa i ławników karany. 37. Żeby się żaden nie ważył i tej nie daję, zagrodnika albo chamocy łupnika czyli komornika do siebie wziąć, albo na rolę swoją wsadzić bez wiadomości całego sąsiedztwa pod karą beczki piwa. 38. Żeby tego potrzeba było dla lepszego [dobra] wsi albo groblę spust czyli rowy dla spustu wód uczynić, czyli też role tamami opatrzyć, powinni się sąsiedzi według hub składać na to, ja [ze].strony mojej przyobiecuję sąsiedzkie wsie do pomocki przybrać. Ktoby się temu sprzeciwiał, powinien według uznania sołtysa i ławników być karany. 39. Sołtys i ławnicy będą obligowani co dwie niedziele, a to w wtorkowy dzień sąsiadom sądy trzymać, skarg słuchać, kłótnie zgadzać, sztrafy jak najpilniej odbierać, tylko żeby strona jedna dzień przed sądem drugiej stronie zawczasu oznajmowała i obstalowała, cudzemu zaś każdego czasu przy zapłacie urzędowej sprawiedliwość uczynić potrzeba. " 40. Przed zejściem sądu powinien skarżący dwanaście groszy cesarskich położyć, z których sołtysowi cztery należą grosze cesarskie. 41. To zaś sobie zachowuję, żeby sołtys miał baczenie dobre, ażeby sprawy kryminalne, sztrafy dworne nie były zatajone. Te się zawsze do mnie będą ferowały i mnie donieść potrzeba sprawy takie. Co się inszych spraw tyczy, oddaję to dla lepszego wsi sądzenia, ile sołtysowi zawsze od okrwawienia i bicia [z] znakami ośm groszy cesarskich powinni oddawać, oprócz [tego] ławnikom ich należącą kwotę. 42. Uskarżając się kto przed sołtysem i ławnikami jego, mając wolę w sprawie swojej do pana pójść, tego jemu pozwolić potrzeba [fol. 10] rozkazuję, ktoby zaś zuchwale i hardym sposobem apelować chciał, powinien być na grzywnę jedną karany. 43. Jeżeliby sąsiad jeden drugiemu chciał majętność czyli cudzemu sprzedać, powinien to pierwej sołtysowi oznajmić, a pokryjomu nie sprzedawać, żeby kto długów po sobie nie zostawił. Czy to pod pa-

</div>
<div class="lit-en" lang="en" markdown="1">

[fol. 9] 34. Geese and ducks, when they stray in and do damage to a neighbour, may be killed and sent back home to their owner.

35. If anyone during a court session hisses at another in discourteous words or plays a trick on him, he is to pay a fine of five groszes; if he threatens blows, he is to go into obedience and pay 10 groszes. And he is not to be released from obedience any sooner until he has come to an agreement with his neighbour and apologised.

36. The wiertel, the quarter and the beer measure are to be measured out fairly according to the measures of the neighbouring towns, so that no one suffers wrong. Whoever acts against this and cheats his neighbour is to be punished at the discretion of the sołtys and the ławniks.

37. No one is to presume — and this I do not allow — to take a smallholder (zagrodnik) or a cottager, that is a lodger, into his own house, or settle him on his land, without the knowledge of the whole neighbourhood, on pain of a barrel of beer.

38. If there is need, for the better good of the village, to make a dam with a sluice, or ditches for draining off the waters, or to provide the fields with dams, the neighbours are to contribute to it according to their hubas; I on my side promise to bring in the neighbouring villages to help. Whoever opposes this is to be punished at the discretion of the sołtys and the ławniks.

39. The sołtys and the ławniks are obliged every two weeks, on a Tuesday, to hold court for the neighbours, hear complaints, settle disputes and collect the fines as diligently as possible; only, one party is to give notice and instruction to the other a day before the court sitting; and for an outsider justice is to be done at any time, on payment of the official fee.

40. Before the court sitting the complainant is to deposit twelve imperial groszes, of which four imperial groszes belong to the sołtys.

41. And this I reserve to myself: that the sołtys is to keep good watch that criminal cases and fines belonging to the lord's court are not concealed. These are always to be brought before me, and such matters must be reported to me. As for the other cases, I entrust them to the sołtys for the better judgement of the village; for wounding and beating [with] marks, eight imperial groszes are always to be paid to the sołtys, besides the amount due to his ławniks.

42. If someone complains before the sołtys and his ławniks and wishes to take his case to the lord, he must be allowed to do so, and this is [fol. 10] ordered; but if anyone wants to appeal presumptuously and insolently, he is to be fined one grzywna.

43. If one neighbour wishes to sell another an estate or property of any kind, he must first notify the sołtys

</div>
</section>

<section class="lit-passage" id="p-156" data-page="156">
<div class="pg" id="p156"><a href="#p156">p. 156</a></div>
<div class="lit-orig" lang="pl" markdown="1">

O nem, czy pod gminą kupujący, zawsze powinien piwa beczkę sąsiadom dać, kupując. Swoi, którzy zawsze bliżsi kupna, i ci powinni beczkę piwa sąsiadom. — 44. Gdyby kto cudzy chciał hubę albo majętność czyjąś kupować, powinien najprzód u sołtysa należytą uczynić wiadomość przy beczce piwa, jeżeli się znajduje sąsiad, który hubę tę może kupić, a jeżeliby się kto taki znajdował [we] wsi, ma przodek kupowania huby tej i do kupna przypuszczony być ma, lecz bliższy kupna tego sąsiad ten, który z hubą sprzedawaną graniczy. Jeżeliby się zaś znajdowali krewni z huby tej, ci najbliżsi do otrzymania huby sprzedawanej, i żadnym sposobem zabraniać im nie potrzeba. Ktoby się temu sprzeciwiał, powinien na pana położyć sztrafy grzywien dobrych dziesięć, a sąsiadom za zuchwałość tę kary beczkę piwa.

Rozkazuję tedy soltysowi i ławnikom serio, ażeby nad pomienionym prawem I sztrafą mocno trzymali i je zachowali pod karą wielką na dwór. Tę ustawę i konstytucję jak najpilniej zachować i wykonać, na przeciw prawom tym nikomu nie pozwalam czynić. Dla wiary 1 konfirmacji doskonalszej pieczęcią przyrodzoną własną wiadomie pieczętuję i podpisuję. Dano w dziedzicznych dobrach moich Żerkowie.

[Daty, pieczęci i podpisu brak. Przywilej lokacyjny wydany został olędrom w r. 1729. Wystawienie niniejszego wilkierza nastąpiło prawdopodobnie w latach najbliższych].

</div>
<div class="lit-en" lang="en" markdown="1">

and not sell it secretly, so that no one leaves debts behind him. Whether it is

under the lord or under the community, the buyer is always to give the neighbours a barrel of beer when he buys. And his own kinsmen, who are always the nearest to the purchase, are also to give the neighbours a barrel of beer. — 44. If anyone wishes to buy another person's huba or anyone's estate, he must first give due notice at the sołtys's, with a barrel of beer; if there is a neighbour who can buy that huba, and such a person is found [in] the village, he is to have precedence in the purchase of this huba and be admitted to the purchase; but the neighbour who borders on the huba being sold has the nearer right of purchase. If there are kinsmen from that huba, they are the nearest to receive the huba being sold, and they are not to be barred from it in any way. Whoever opposes this is to pay to the lord a fine of ten good grzywny, and to the neighbours, for this presumption, a barrel of beer by way of penalty.

I therefore earnestly command the sołtys and the ławniks to hold firmly to the said law and its penalties and to keep them, on pain of severe penalty from the manor. This statute and constitution is to be kept and carried out as diligently as possible; I permit no one to act against these laws. For surer assurance and confirmation I seal with my own natural seal knowingly and sign. Given in my hereditary estate of Żerków.

[The date, seal and signature are lacking. The founding charter was granted to the Olęders in 1729. The issue of the present wilkierz probably followed in the years nearest to it.]

## Władysław Rusiński, *Osady tzw. „olędrów" w dawnym województwie poznańskim* — English translation

> **Translator's note.** This is a translation of the monograph  
> (Poznań 1939, Kraków 1947). Conventions, agreed with the editor:  
> British spelling; the ethnic term **Olęder(s)** (Pol. *olędrzy*,  
> German *Hauländer*) is retained and glossed at first use; archival  
> sigla (AW., Rel. Posn., Tp. 89 …), archive call marks and  
> bibliographic titles are kept in their original form; numbers  
> follow the print exactly, with Polish thousand/decimal separators  
> converted to the English convention (13.737 → 13,737; 6,05 → 6.05)  
> and no value altered — including the print's own internal  
> discrepancies; measures are glossed at first use; quotations from  
> archival Polish are translated, the original wording being given  
> only where the author discusses it; quotations in German keep the  
> original with a translation; the tables of ANEKS I are not  
> translated in this edition. The bracketed `[p. N]` markers are the  
> print's own pagination.  
>  
> **Terms used.** *Olęder(s)* — one of the Dutch-origin farming  
> colonists and their settlements (Pol. *olędrzy/olędry*, German  
> *Hauländer*); "Ol. X" = an Olęder settlement named X. *huba*  
> (pl. *hubas*) — a full hide, the basic holding unit (cf. German  
> *Hufe*). *włóka* (pl. *włókas*) — the field measure (in this book  
> the 30-morg włóka). *morg* (pl. *morgs*) — a land measure. *dym* —  
> hearth, the fiscal unit (the hearth tax = *podymne*). *tymf* — the  
> debased Polish coin of the late 17th and early 18th century.  
> *folwark* — manor farm. *sołtys* — village headman. *ławnik* —  
> lay assessor (juror). *wolnizna* — a rent-free period granted at  
> settlement. *wilkierz* — a village by-law. *oblaty* — enrolments  
> of documents in the court books. *wieś zaciężna* — a contract  
> village settled under Polish law. *chałupnik* — a cottage dweller  
> without land. *komornik* — a lodger. *zagrodnik* — a smallholder  
> with a garden plot. *starostwo* — a royal domain held by a  
> starosta. *królewszczyzny* — royal estates. *majętność* — a  
> private estate complex. *serwituty* — servitudes (rights of use).  
> *szarwark* — corvée labour. *robocizna* — labour due. *przymus  
> mlewa* — the milling monopoly. *propinacja* — the propination  
> (liquor) monopoly. *pogłówne* — poll tax. *hyberna* — the winter  
> levy. *korzec/garniec* — dry measures (pl. *korcy/garnce*).
